**European Cup / UEFA Champions League – clubs with the five‑highest title tallies (as of the 2023‑24 season)**  

| Rank (by titles) | Club | UEFA Champions‑League / European Cup titles* | Current home ground (2025) | Stadium capacity (approx.) | Source |
|------------------|------|---------------------------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|--------|
| 1 | **Real Madrid CF** | **14** titles (1956‑60, 1966, 1998, 2000, 2002, 2014, 2016‑18, 2022, 2023) | **Estadio Santiago Bernabéu** – Madrid | 81,044 | <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF#European_success> |
| 2 | **AC Milan** | **7** titles (1963, 1969, 1989, 1990, 1994, 2003, 2007) | **Stadio Giuseppe Meazza (San Siro)** – Milan (shared with Inter Milan) | 75,817 | <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan#European_success> |
| 3 | **Liverpool FC** | **6** titles (1977, 1978, 1981, 1984, 2005, 2019) | **Anfield** – Liverpool | 53,394 | <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_FC#European_success> |
| 4 | **FC Bayern Munich** | **6** titles (1974‑76, 2001, 2013, 2020) | **Allianz Arena** – Munich | 75,000 | <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich#European_success> |
| 5 | **FC Barcelona** | **5** titles (1992, 2006, 2009, 2011, 2015) | **Camp Nou** – Barcelona | 99,354 | <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona#European_success> |

\*The counts include the competition’s full history – the European Cup (1955‑1992) and its successor, the UEFA Champions League (1992‑present).  

### Quick notes on the stadiums
- **Estadio Santiago Bernabéu** – undergoing a major renovation (2023‑2025) but remains Real Madrid’s primary home ground.  
- **Stadio Giuseppe Meazza (San Siro)** – still the shared venue for AC Milan and Inter Milan; a new separate stadium for AC Milan is planned for the late‑2020s but has not opened yet.  
- **Anfield** – Liverpool’s historic ground; a modest expansion completed in 2022 increased capacity to ~53 k.  
- **Allianz Arena** – purpose‑built for Bayern Munich (opened 2005); also used by the German national team for occasional fixtures.  
- **Camp Nou** – Barcelona’s iconic stadium; a redevelopment project (Espai Barça) is in progress, with the core stadium expected to be modernised but still operational as of 2025.  

These five clubs together account for **38** of the 61 UEFA Champions‑League/European‑Cup titles awarded to date, making them the most successful clubs in the competition’s history.
